title: URTC CAN protocol
about: Machine-readable specification of the CAN bus protocol of the URTC tool head: every identifier with its direction, length rule and payload layout, the magic payloads, the registers of the expansion slave, the version procedures and the SLCAN subset the host tools rely on. All multi-byte fields are big-endian.

version_query.title: Version query
version_query.rule: Application major.minor.patch is (0x7F9 major, 0x7F9 minor, 0x7E9 patch). Without 0x7E9 within the grace window the patch is unknown and the legacy two-component form is used.

minor_field.title: Minor field of the end-of-update frame
minor_field.rule: Legacy: the minor. With a patch (0 to 127), only towards a bootloader that announced bit 0 of the flags of 0x7E9: ((0x80 | patch) << 8) | minor.

version_order.title: Anti-rollback order
version_order.rule: Major, then minor; the patch takes part only when both versions carry one.

slcan.title: SLCAN subset that is relied on
slcan.frame: t + 3 hex digits of identifier + 1 hex digit of DLC (0 to 8) + 2 hex digits per data byte
rules: Only standard (11-bit) data frames are carried; T, r and R lines are discarded.
Every character after the leading t must be a hexadecimal digit: a sign, a 0x prefix or an underscore is not.
A DLC above 8 is not a CAN 2.0 frame.
The line length must equal 5 + 2 * DLC exactly; a truncated payload, trailing characters and adapter timestamps are all discarded.
Status characters (z, Z after a transmit, BELL on a bus error) may precede a frame in the same buffered line: the frame is the text from the first t or T on.
A receive buffer that grows beyond 4096 bytes without a terminator is discarded.
Lines that are not ASCII are discarded.

messages.name: SLAVE_REG_WRITE
messages.title: Write a slave application register (generic)
notes: Implemented by the firmware; no host implements it. Writes an arbitrary application register of the expansion slave, with no magic payload and no allow-list: a security gap to close before any host sends it (see docs/CONTRACTS.md).

messages.name: SLAVE_REG_READ
messages.title: Read a slave application register (generic)
notes: Implemented by the firmware; no host implements it. Reads one application register of the expansion slave, from the closed list of registers the firmware relays (anything else is dropped without an answer). The version register (0x01) is read whole: its tenth byte, the PATCH number of the slave application, follows in 0x222.

messages.name: SLAVE_APP_PATCH
messages.title: Patch number of the slave application (companion of 0x221)

fields.name: register
fields.note: The register the patch belongs to: 0x01, the version register of the slave application.

notes: TX-only; nothing on the board listens for it. Sent right after the 0x221 answer for register 0x01 when the tenth byte of that register, the patch number of the slave application, is 1 to 127. A byte of 0 (what a slave application from before the field sends) is ignored and no frame follows, so a host that sees no 0x222 treats the patch as unknown.

messages.name: END_UPDATE

messages.name: HEARTBEAT

notes: Sent only by the bootloader, alongside 0x7F9. Released flashers read it only at exactly DLC 3.

messages.title: Authorise a downgrade for the current update
notes: One-shot: reset at every 0x7F1 and consumed by the anti-rollback check of the next 0x7F4. The image must still be validly signed.

Answered only in a bootloader session that the application started by accepting 0x7F0, or when no valid application is installed (a recovery); in any other session the frame is ignored. A build option switches the restriction off.

messages.name: READBACK
messages.title: Read back the installed application

fields.name: total_size
fields.note: 0 when nothing valid is installed.

Raw bytes of the main slot, eight per frame; the prose says eight, but the last frame is as short as the size requires.

notes: One 2048-byte page (256 frames), then the bootloader waits up to 3 s for the page acknowledgement 0x7FF.

Answered only in a bootloader session that the application started by accepting 0x7F0, or when no valid application is installed (a recovery); in any other session the frame is ignored. A build option switches the restriction off.

multinode.title: Several tool heads on one bus
multinode.about: A backward-compatible extension that lets several tool heads share one CAN bus. The URTC firmware implements the node side behind a persistent switch that is off by default (0x1AC sets it, 0x1AD reads it, a change acts after the next power-up); with the switch off the board behaves exactly as a single head. The logic is tested on the host; it has not been tried on boards, and no host program uses it yet. The frames of the single-head protocol keep their identifiers and meaning; the extension only uses identifiers that nothing else uses (0x400-0x49F). See docs/MULTINODE.md.

node_address.source: The five identity jumpers ID0-ID4 that the firmware reads once at boot (the tool address, 0 to 31). Two heads of the same tool type on one bus need a different instance number or are refused as a conflict.

constants.name: MN_NODE_TIMEOUT_MS
constants.title: A node that sent no status frame for this long is treated as gone

constants.name: MN_SELECT_TIMEOUT_MS
constants.title: A selection lapses unless the host repeats it within this time

constants.name: MN_LEGACY_LISTEN_MS
constants.title: A node listens this long after start for other nodes before it behaves as the one head on the bus

constants.name: MN_CMD_ARGS_MAX
constants.title: Argument bytes that fit in a node-addressed command

state_flags.name: SELECTED
state_flags.title: This node is the selected (active) node

state_flags.name: FAULT
state_flags.title: A fault is latched on this node

state_flags.name: CONFLICT
state_flags.title: Another node answered with the same address: this node ignores commands

frames.name: DISCOVER
frames.title: Ask every node to announce itself
notes: Every node answers with MN_NODE_INFO after address times slot_ms, so the answers never collide.

frames.name: SELECT
frames.title: Select the one node that the single-head frames address
notes: Only the selected node obeys the identifiers of the single-head protocol; the others stay silent on them. A selection lapses after MN_SELECT_TIMEOUT_MS unless it is repeated.
seq is recorded and not otherwise interpreted. A frame that is malformed (wrong length, action above 1, node above 31) changes nothing.

frames.name: SAFE_STOP
frames.title: Ask every node to enter its safe state
notes: A request to move toward safety, never away from it: a node always obeys it and leaves the safe state only through its own conditions.

frames.name: NODE_INFO
frames.title: A node announces itself (identifier plus the node address)
notes: Sent after DISCOVER and once at start. Two nodes that send the same identifier with different data cause a bus error on the data bits; both then set CONFLICT.

frames.name: NODE_STATUS
frames.title: Periodic status of one node
notes: Sent every MN_STATUS_PERIOD_MS by every node, selected or not. This is the heartbeat the host uses to notice a node that is gone.

frames.name: NODE_CMD
frames.title: One command to one node without selecting it

examples.name: global status, two bytes of arguments

notes: func is the identifier of a single-head command. Commands whose payload is longer than MN_CMD_ARGS_MAX bytes use SELECT and the single-head frames instead.
The firmware answers only func 0x110 (the status query, answered with the six bytes of 0x111); any other func is ignored, so this short form never actuates.

frames.name: NODE_RESP
frames.title: The answer of one node to NODE_CMD
notes: func repeats the identifier of the command that is answered.

multinode.status_title: implemented in the firmware behind a switch that is off by default, tested on the host only
